analysis: What changed vs the 4:00 AM brief: the morning's own earnings wave split the same way last night's did — beats are not enough on their own. Eli Lilly blew past forecasts (revenue $24.4B, adjusted EPS $7.48) and raised its full-year revenue outlook to $91-92B, and shares rose ~4.3% premarket. Caterpillar also beat (adjusted EPS $7.20, revenue $20.7B, margin up 310 bps) but merely maintained full-year guidance, and shares fell ~9% premarket — the mirror image, and a reminder that a beat with no raise is being sold in this tape. That extends the 4 AM theme: Alphabet still down ~10% premarket on negative $9.07B free cash flow, with the new detail that AI Mode searches monetize worse than traditional search (ads in AI Mode only went worldwide today), while Microsoft's cash-flow-backed beat keeps it up ~3.5% as the offset. Signal: the market is now grading earnings on cash conversion and guidance raises, not beats alone — and the AI-capex scrutiny has spread from hyperscalers into chips (SOXX -2.5%) and AI-linked industrials like Caterpillar's power business. Noise: the Marvell/Lumentum talks remain a single Bloomberg report with no company comment, and the Vance letter to Iran is still a reported overture, not a deal. Into the open, everything funnels into 8:30 a.m. ET GDP (consensus ~+3.2% annualized) and core PCE (+0.3% m/m expected), which feed directly into the ~84% December-hike pricing, plus the ECB decision and Amazon/Intel after the close.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures stay split into the open: Nasdaq 100 futures -1%, S&P 500 futures -0.3%, Dow futures +0.1% in recent trading, with Alphabet still dragging tech lower while the Dow holds up.
headlines.why_it_matters: Same shape as the 4 AM read — a tech-led soft open, not broad risk-off, with the Dow's lower tech weight cushioning it.

headlines.headline: Eli Lilly crushes Q3 and raises guidance: revenue $24.4B (+39% YoY) vs ~$22.5B expected, adjusted EPS $7.48 vs ~$5.6-5.7 expected; Mounjaro $10.7B (+65%) and Zepbound $5.35B both beat; full-year revenue outlook raised to $91-92B from $85-87B, though adjusted EPS guidance trimmed to $35-36 on a $4.2B in-process R&D charge. Shares +4.3% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh this morning — a beat plus a raise is still being rewarded, and it gives the premarket a non-tech offset to Alphabet's drag.

headlines.headline: Caterpillar beats but sinks ~9% premarket: Q3 revenue $20.7B (+17% YoY) vs ~$20.5B expected, adjusted EPS $7.20 vs ~$7.1 expected, adjusted operating margin up 310 bps to 20.6%, enterprise operating cash flow $4.4B — but the company only maintained full-year guidance, and its power business sits in the middle of the AI-spending scrutiny.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh this morning — the mirror image of Lilly: a beat with no raise is being sold, which is a headwind for the Dow's industrial leg into the open.

headlines.headline: Alphabet still ~10% lower premarket after Q3, with a new detail from the call: chief business officer Philipp Schindler said AI Mode searches monetize at a lower rate than traditional search, and Google only began showing ads alongside AI Mode worldwide today (previously US-tested only); CFO said 2026 capex of $195-205B stands and 2027 spending rises significantly, with near-term margin pressure from third-party cloud capacity.
headlines.why_it_matters: Carried from the 4 AM brief but still the tape's main weight — the monetization detail explains why the ads miss stings more than the cloud doubling helps.

headlines.headline: Microsoft still ~3.5% higher premarket on its fiscal Q1 beat (revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, $18.6B free cash flow despite $45.2B capex); the Wall Street Journal also reported Microsoft plans buyouts this week with about 60,000 of its 223,000 employees potentially eligible.
headlines.why_it_matters: The standing offset to Alphabet — cash-backed cloud growth is still what the market pays up for, and the buyout report adds a cost-discipline read.

headlines.headline: Chips soften further: Nvidia -0.92% premarket, SOXX -2.5%, memory ETF DRAM down nearly 4% after jumping 7% Wednesday; Marvell -10% on a Bloomberg report it is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum (+4.3%) — neither company has commented.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed on the Marvell/Lumentum talks — treat that leg as fragile, but the chip softness fits the AI-capex de-risking into the open.

headlines.headline: Other megacaps mixed premarket: Apple +0.83%, Meta +0.90%, Amazon -0.71% ahead of its after-close report, Tesla -0.99%; the MAGS ETF was ~1% lower premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: No new company news behind these moves — they are riding the Alphabet-led tech tape, with Amazon's after-close print the next stock-specific test.

headlines.headline: Merck +3% premarket after Q3: profit $5.07B ($2.04/share) vs $5.79B ($2.32) a year earlier, with revenue up on Keytruda and Winrevair growth.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh this morning — a second healthcare offset alongside Lilly, cushioning the Dow while tech slides.

headlines.headline: Macro into the open: US Q3 GDP (consensus ~+3.2% annualized) and September PCE (core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y expected) plus jobless claims all land at 8:30 a.m. ET; the ECB decision follows (hold at a 2.50% deposit rate expected). Traders price ~84% odds of a December Fed hike after yesterday's 10-2 hold at 3.75-4.00%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The data, not earnings, decides the rate story today — a hot print feeds the December-hike pricing the Fed just kept alive.
